teaser_de: Fünf Mitglieder des Niner Empire Germany haben sich intensiv mit dem Draft beschäftigt und ihre Mock Drafts für die 49ers erstellt.
teaser_en: Five members of Niner Empire Germany dug deep into the draft and put together their 49ers mock drafts.
body_en:
![NEG mock draft 2026](https://i0.wp.com/theninerempiregermany.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mock_draft_final.png?resize=772%2C422&ssl=1)

The 2026 NFL Draft is just around the corner, and here at Niner Empire Germany the excitement grows every day! Five of our members have studied this year's draft class intensively and locked in their picks in a secret ballot as part of a mock draft: Who will it be? Who should it be? And which bold predictions do they dare to make?

The excitement is especially big this time: Lukas, Lars and our David, [the reigning San Francisco 49ers International Fan of the Year](https://theninerempiregermany.de/international-fan-of-the-year-2025/), won't be following the draft from the couch but will experience it live on site in Pittsburgh. Three Niners from Germany, right in the middle of the action!

For everyone following along at home: here are our panel's assessments, so you are well prepared when Roger Goodell steps up to the podium. Let's go!

### The panel

Lukas, Miron and David formed their opinions through intensive tape work and analyze the prospects directly on the field; Lars and Chris bring the outside perspective and base their assessments on the expertise of leading NFL podcasts and specialist media.

### Method and voting

In a secret ballot, each panelist submitted a prediction pick (what he expects) and a wish pick (what he hopes for) for round 1 and round 2, plus a wish pick for day 3 and a hot take or bold prediction for this year's draft: a mock draft of sorts.

### The picks

### Round 1

| Panelist | Prediction pick | Wish pick |
|---|---|---|
| Lars | Caleb Lomu, OT, Utah. The 49ers treat themselves to the luxury of picking their future LT at 27. In a weak draft class, the Niners gamble on upside and hope he can replace Trent Williams in the long run. Lomu still needs to work on his technique but physically brings everything needed for the tackle position. | Kenyon Sadiq, TE, Oregon. Young, dynamic and the perfect George Kittle successor or the perfect complement. Sadiq needs to develop as a blocker, but as a pass catcher he will be a huge weapon for Kyle Shanahan from day 1. At just 21, the Kittle replacement would be ready for years to come; his athleticism is unmatched. |
| Lukas | Malachi Lawrence, EDGE, UCF. The 49ers love drafting edge rushers in the first round, and Malachi Lawrence fits the profile. Good mass; he can immediately be the pass-rush specialist opposite Nick Bosa. Malachi Lawrence was also at a top-30 visit in Santa Clara. | KC Concepcion, WR, Texas A&M. KC Concepcion is the best separator in the draft and would bring a new vertical element to the offense with his speed. KC has few weaknesses and would be an immediate asset for the offense. |
| Miron | KC Concepcion, WR, Texas A&M. He is a versatile weapon who can be used in the slot, outside or in the backfield, and he shines especially with his yards after the catch (YAC) in the short passing game. Top-30 visit with us and simply looks like a perfect match. | Kadyn Proctor, OL, Alabama. Simply a fascinating prospect in my eyes: age, measurables and upside. Put him in the starting lineup at LG and let him learn from Trent Williams before he takes over at left tackle. My draft crush for quite some time. |
| Chris | Malachi Lawrence, EDGE, UCF. As a confirmed non-tape-watcher, I have to rely on trustworthy sources. And what Greg Cosell and Bruce Feldman have said about Malachi Lawrence fits this year's Niners approach perfectly: use the offseason to round out the roster, then take a high-risk, high-reward approach in the draft (some would call it a reach). Malachi Lawrence fits that perfectly. Ranked somewhere between the late 30s and early 50s on most boards, but with brutal traits (a top-13 RAS score among all DEs ever) and a quick get-off, exactly what Kocurek wants. | Max Iheanachor, OT, Arizona State. As everyone knows, Trent Williams isn't getting any younger, and it's slowly time to look for his successor. Thanks to a good offseason, the roster is set up so that there is no real need, so the team can finally address the OT position. From what you hear, Max offers exactly what Trent gave us for years: explosiveness in the run game, stability in the passing game, just not fully developed yet (he has only been playing football since 2021). That's why someone like him will hopefully fall into our range, and we can take the chance to develop him behind Trent for another year. |
| David | Kadyn Proctor, OT, Alabama. Despite an agreement with Trent Williams, the 49ers will take an offensive tackle at pick 27 with Kadyn Proctor, provided he is still on the board. A project: the future at OT will take priority over an impact in the 2026 season. | Avieon Terrell, CB, Clemson. With Terrell, we would get a starting-caliber corner and a real ballhawk. Thanks to free agency, our offense is already very well set up for the coming season, and I would simply like us to get an impact player for the defense. |

### Round 2

| Panelist | Prediction pick | Wish pick |
|---|---|---|
| Lars | Chris Brazzell, WR, Tennessee. Brazzell is an incredible athlete who will have a hard time in the Shanahan doghouse at first. But once he knows how to use his body as a WR and as a blocker, he will be unstoppable. That's what the 49ers gamble on in round 2. | Treydan Stukes, DB, Arizona. Stukes is an all-purpose weapon in the defensive backfield. His production speaks for itself, but he spent six years in college overall and had injury problems. He is described as a leader; the coaches will love him. A belated candidate to succeed Jimmie Ward. |
| Lukas | Bud Clark, S, TCU. The 49ers find what they are looking for in a starting safety and select S Bud Clark from TCU. Raheem Morris gets his preferred player and one of the best coverage safeties in this draft. | Treydan Stukes, DB, Arizona. Treydan Stukes is already 25, but he brings everything needed to be an impact player from day 1. Stukes has incredible speed, is excellent in coverage and can play practically any position in the defensive backfield. |
| Miron | Romello Height, EDGE, Texas Tech. Pass-rush specialist. Against the run it gets thinner. An exciting prospect nonetheless! | Bryce Lance, WR, NDSU. Just for the fun of it! But a good prospect beyond that as well. Depends a lot on whether we already take a receiver in the first round. |
| Chris | Germie Bernard, WR, Alabama. This would be what everyone describes as the safe option at WR: he can play everything and is ready right away. Since all our WRs except Pearsall are on short contracts or still complete question marks, I think the team would happily go the safe route here, if he is still available, and get a building block for the next two years. | Chris Bell, WR, Louisville. I think the team should continue the high-risk, high-reward approach here and try to get one of the top-4 WRs who only fell because of an ACL injury. Ideally via a trade-up with one of the fourth-rounders. It's no secret that Shanahan was a big fan of AJ Brown (only a bigger one of Deebo Samuel), and now he would have the chance to get such a dynamic receiver again. The advantage would be that Bell would have time to recover, since the WR room is currently full, with the prospect of getting a true WR1. |
| David | to follow | to follow |

### Day 3: wish pick

| Panelist | Wish pick (day 3) |
|---|---|
| Lars | Sam Roush, TE, Stanford. If the Niners don't go with Sadiq in round 1, Sam Roush would be my choice, also from a local point of view. At the combine, he was the only TE to complete every test and looked great doing it. Willing blocker, good receiver; production was a bit lacking. Who does that remind you of? This time for real… |
| Lukas | Genesis Smith, S, Arizona. For me, Smith is one of the best coverage safeties in this draft. He is a playmaker, has enough speed and can play single-high safety at the next level without any problems. On the other hand, he has big problems tackling against the run. |
| Miron | Jack Endries, TE, Texas. Former Cal tight end. Good all-around package with development potential. |
| Chris | Diego Pavia, QB, Vanderbilt. Admittedly, round 3 is a bit early, but I'll interpret it as a wish player for day 3. I followed Pavia all year after the Netflix SEC documentary, and I find his style of play simply fun. Probably too small for a QB, but at Jon Gruden's QB school he already said he'd play anything if necessary. Maybe a Taysom Hill-like Swiss Army knife? |
| David | to follow |

### Hot takes and bold predictions

**Lars:** The 49ers won't hold back in the draft. It wouldn't shock me if they traded up several times.

**Lukas:** Raheem Morris gets control of the first-round pick and selects safety Bud Clark from TCU. In addition, the 49ers wait until late on day 3 to take a WR: Caleb Douglas from Texas Tech.

**Miron:** We'll make more than one trade-up!

**Chris:** A trade-up with the Jets (including Brandon Aiyuk) to pick Jordyn Tyson at No. 16.

**David:** We will see two 49ers trades in this draft, because we have too many picks at the end of the fourth round and will try to get our targets.

### Conclusion and outlook

The offensive line dominates our panel's thinking: Trent Williams' succession is the topic of this draft for many. At the same time, the wish picks show that the Niners fan base is hungry: for impact players on both sides of the ball, for bold moves and for a draft that really makes a difference!

And that's exactly what we expect from Lynch and Shanahan: no waiting, no just managing, but full throttle! Our panel's hot takes certainly suggest that a lot could happen in Pittsburgh. We are ready. Go Niners!
